description: We are Capy Tinkering, a team united by curiosity and a passion for science and technology. We combine different skills and perspectives to explore questions, test ideas, and build creative solutions. Our approach is learning by doing: researching, experimenting, and improving together. We value collaboration, inclusion, and sharing knowledge, with each member contributing to the path from a question to a solution.
summary:
Team Capy Tinkering developed Mission Capybara, a 3D educational game prototype that invites students to plan a scientific mission to the Moon alongside a crew of capybara astronauts. Players explore gravity, assemble a modular rocket, design a scientific satellite, and investigate how to reach the Moon and conduct research on its surface.
The project addresses the challenge of designing a space science mission by turning physics and engineering concepts into gameplay decisions. As players select engines, fuel tanks, and scientific instruments, they consider how mass, available power, and research goals shape mission design. NASA resources connect these activities to real-world space science.
Mission Capybara makes space engineering more accessible to children and teens by giving them a chance to test their ideas and see how each choice affects the mission.
details:
Mission Capybara, developed by Team Capy Tinkering for the Space Mission Design Game challenge of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, is an educational digital project combining an interactive presentation website with a space exploration and mission planning game. Its purpose is to bring science, aerospace engineering, and lunar exploration closer to children, teenagers, families, and educators through a playful, investigative, and collaborative experience.
The project features a fictional Brazilian capybara family as the protagonists of a scientific journey to the Moon. The narrative begins with questions about lunar mysteries and guides participants through scientific investigation, the understanding of space concepts, and decision making related to mission planning.

The game offers two complementary experiences. The first, Tycho Expedition, consists of six chapters covering gravity, launch vehicles, scientific instruments, orbits, lunar missions, and lunar science. In this mode, players explore scientific concepts, compare instruments, and interpret published evidence, developing scientific reasoning and investigative skills.
The second experience, Resource Mission, allows players to plan and manage a lunar mission. Players must select a scientific objective, choose equipment, and configure systems such as cameras, power, communications, and fuel while respecting mass, budget, and energy constraints. During mission operations, players perform simplified maneuvers, manage fuel, collect and store scientific data, and use available communication opportunities to transmit information back to Earth. Each decision has consequences for mission performance, helping players understand the relationship between engineering, planning, and resource management.
The website complements the game by presenting its story, objectives, characters, participation guidelines, and scientific references, including publicly available materials from NASA, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), and the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) team.

The project distinguishes published scientific information from simplified models and educational rules developed to make the experience accessible and interactive.
The main benefits include encouraging critical thinking, problem solving, creativity, logical reasoning, collaboration, and interdisciplinary learning. The project transforms complex scientific and engineering concepts into accessible challenges in which participants learn through experimentation, analysis, and the continuous improvement of their strategies.
Inclusion is one of the project’s core principles. The capybara family consists of four characters with different areas of expertise: Luna, responsible for science and discovery; Iara, focused on construction and energy; Capi, responsible for flight and orbits; and Bento, focused on communications and resources, represented as a wheelchair user. The narrative values different abilities and demonstrates that everyone can contribute to scientific discoveries and engineering decisions. The project also incorporates accessibility features such as text enlargement, a calm mode, and animation pause controls, aiming to provide a more comfortable and inclusive experience.
The development combines digital experience creation tools, programming, interface design, illustration, and technological resources to build the website and game.

The website was developed using the Lovable platform. The game is implemented as an interactive digital experience published on the web. Its technological architecture integrates user interfaces, visual elements, storytelling, scientific content, and educational simulation mechanics. Scientific data serve as references, while certain operational parameters are simplified for educational purposes.
The project’s main creative aspect is the combination of an original narrative featuring Brazilian capybaras, space exploration, challenge-based learning, and simulated engineering decisions. Rather than simply presenting information about the Moon, the project places participants in the role of members of a team responsible for planning and carrying out a mission, helping them understand how each decision can influence the final outcome.

Throughout development, the team considered the accuracy and reliability of scientific references, content clarity, player experience, accessibility, collaboration, challenge balance, usability, compatibility across different devices, and the distinction between real scientific data and educational models.

The intended impact is to increase interest in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM), democratize access to space education, and encourage children and teenagers to see themselves as future scientists, researchers, and engineers. Mission Capybara demonstrates that space exploration can be understood and experienced through curiosity, creativity, collaboration, and scientific knowledge.
